findings.description: The eval_only refusal derives the protected property with a strict JSON comparison (`.toggles.oracle_open == true`), but the consumer of that same toggle in the same file uses the loose `jq -r '.oracle_open'` text comparison at line 348, which also matches the YAML string "true". An arm declared as `toggles: {oracle_open: "true"}` therefore plans/opens the mount (overlay=none(oracle_open)) while EVAL_ONLY stays false, so the run is not refused outside a batch and no `eval_only:` line is printed. lib/sandbox-mount.sh is not in the diff, but pipeline-run.sh and the stub use the same `jq -r` pattern for every other toggle, so the real overlay path very likely accepts the string too. validate-suite.sh does reject the string form, but pipeline-run.sh does not invoke the validator, so the runtime guard alone is what protects against this and it is bypassable with a one-character suite edit (quoting). The comment at 259-261 states the intent (DISS-C-002: derive from the property) that this predicate mismatch defeats.
findings.failure_mode: The review-catch oracle is opened for a direct manual pipeline-run.sh invocation that the FR-5 guard was specifically meant to refuse; rows from an open-oracle run land in a results root without the eval_only marking.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse any present `toggles.oracle_open` that is not a JSON boolean, exactly as `eval_only` is refused at 262-265, and compute EVAL_ONLY with the same expression the mount path uses (or make the mount path use the strict `== true`). Add a bats case for `oracle_open: "true"` asserting exit 2.

findings.cross_file_justification: run-ablation.sh (diff-touched, lines 1300-1301) unconditionally grants LOA_ABLATION_BATCH_CONTEXT=1 to every trial it launches, including smoke, regardless of arm. So inside a batch pipeline-run.sh runs any arm, and the only thing that keeps an open-oracle arm out of the shipped-default decision is ablation-report.py's `components` filter.
findings.description: ablation-report.py excludes an arm from `components` (and so from decisions and the expected-false-positive count) only when `eval_only is True`. It does not apply the DISS-C-002 hardening that pipeline-run.sh received: deriving evaluation-only status from `toggles.oracle_open is True` as well. If a suite declares `oracle_open: true` without `eval_only: true` (validate-suite.sh flags this, but nothing in the diff shows run-ablation.sh or the report invoking the validator), run-ablation.sh's blanket batch context lets pipeline-run.sh run it, and the report then treats the open-oracle arm as a regular component. Its contaminated rows feed a shipped-default decision and render_decisions, while the `eval_only_line` reports "none".
findings.failure_mode: A decision about shipping a review-gate configuration is made on rows where the agent could read the answer paths; the report affirmatively claims there are no evaluation-only arms.
findings.suggested_fix: In build(), compute eval_only per arm as `a.get("eval_only") is True or (a.get("toggles") or {}).get("oracle_open") is True`, use it for both `components` and `eval_only_arms`, and `raise Fail` when an arm opens the oracle without `eval_only: true` so the report refuses rather than silently misclassifying. Optionally have run-ablation.sh run validate-suite.sh on the suite file before launching trials.

findings.description: The "evaluation batch" context is an unauthenticated environment variable. Any wrapper, CI job, or shell that has `LOA_ABLATION_BATCH_CONTEXT=1` in its environment satisfies the guard, and the header text itself instructs operators to set it for dry runs. If an operator uses `export` instead of the documented prefix form, the guard is disabled for every subsequent manual pipeline-run.sh call in that session. run-ablation.sh also grants the context to every trial rather than only to arms the suite marks eval_only, so the variable does not actually encode "this arm was approved for this batch"; it encodes "some runner launched me". This is fine as an accident guard but should not be described as a refusal boundary.
findings.failure_mode: Accidental or inherited environment state silently turns off the only runtime check that keeps the open-oracle arm out of ad-hoc runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer an explicit argv flag (e.g. `--batch-context <batch-id>`) passed by run-ablation.sh and required by pipeline-run.sh for eval_only arms; argv is not inherited across shells. Alternatively, have run-ablation.sh set the variable only for arms whose suite entry is eval_only, and have pipeline-run.sh record the batch id into meta/arm-evidence.txt so took-effect.sh can verify the run came from a batch.
